items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4201

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the highway law, in relation to designating a portion
of state route 38 as the New York State Vietnam Veterans' Memorial
Highway of Valor


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To honor the eight million Americans who served our country during the
Vietnam War era and, more particularly, to honor the 400,000 New
Yorkers that served in our nation's armed forces during that era and
to raise public consciousness about their service and sacrifice with
the re-naming of a portion of state route 38.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill designates a portion of state route 38, from the point where
it intersects with route one hundred four -a in the north thence in a
generally southerly direction to the point of intersection with state
route ninety-six, as the New York State Vietnam Veterans' Memorial
Highway of Valor.

 JUSTIFICATION :
By some estimates, nearly half the men and women that served our
nation during the Vietnam War era are now deceased. Many died without
receiving the recognition that their nation truly appreciated their
service and their sacrifice.  In more recent years, Americans have set
aside their views of the Vietnam War to recognize that it is just,
fitting and proper that we honor these veterans in the same manner as
veterans of other wars and conflicts. Other areas of the state have
done so with fitting tributes. The Cayuga County Legislature now
suggests that to re-name this portion of route 38 is particularly
appropriate since it passes the final resting place of Congressional
Medal of Honor recipient Specialist Robert F. Stryker, an Auburn
native who was killed in action in Loc Ninh, Vietnam in 1967. The
section of highway proposed to be re-named would also be near the home
of Lauren Dates who served with the U.S.  Army's 173rd Airborne
Brigade from February 1967 to February 1968 and was awarded the Combat
Infantryman Badge and the Bronze Star Medal.  This small gesture will
go a long way to say to every Vietnam Veteran and each such veteran's
family, that a grateful state and nation appreciates your service.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
None - new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
Minimal - the cost of appropriate signage.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately upon enactment.
